headline: Highest risk is medium data leakage: Perplexity uploads documents and browsing context while awesome-nlp has no runtime isolation or execution surface to constrain what gets shared.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No direct shared channel is documented between awesome-nlp and Perplexity, so prompt injection is not a default pathway. The only plausible bridge is manual copy-paste or user-mediated transfer into Perplexity’s browsing context or uploaded files. That makes the blast radius small and the interaction unusual rather than inherent.
conditions: IF the user manually copies content from awesome-nlp into Perplexity prompts or uploads it as a file, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared workspace or MCP bridge is added later, the risk increases.
mitigations: Avoid pasting untrusted repo text into Perplexity prompts.
Review any copied content before submission.
Keep the pair disconnected from shared clipboard or shared workspace features.
Use Perplexity only for summaries of trusted, pre-reviewed text.
requires-engineering: add provenance labeling for copied content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Perplexity explicitly touches uploaded documents and browsing context, while awesome-nlp is a docs-only open-source artifact with no runtime isolation or data-handling controls. If the user feeds sensitive material into Perplexity, that material can enter vendor-hosted processing; awesome-nlp does not mitigate or compartmentalize that flow. The pathway exists in default use once documents are uploaded.
conditions: IF the user uploads sensitive documents to Perplexity, those contents are processed in vendor-hosted browsing/search context.
IF the user expects awesome-nlp to provide isolation, that expectation is unsupported by its profile.
mitigations: Do not upload secrets or regulated data to Perplexity.
Use redacted or synthetic documents for analysis.
Restrict Perplexity to non-sensitive search queries.
Separate sensitive work into a different toolchain.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP or upload allowlists.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-nlp has no execution or write capabilities, while Perplexity cannot write files, modify git state, or execute shell commands. Their mutable-resource overlap is therefore minimal. The only shared surface is user-facing content, so conflict risk is limited to coordination mistakes rather than direct state corruption.
conditions: IF a separate orchestrator gives both agents write access outside these profiles, conflict risk would rise.
IF the user manually transfers outputs into a mutable system, coordination errors become possible.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only in the workflow.
Avoid using Perplexity outputs as direct edit instructions.
Do not connect either agent to shared writable repositories.
Review any proposed changes manually before applying them.
requires-engineering: add locking for any future shared mutable resource.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Perplexity is a search-RAG system that can render or act on retrieved content, and awesome-nlp is a curated NLP resource that may be treated as authoritative reference material. If outputs from awesome-nlp are copied into Perplexity prompts, Perplexity may propagate errors or overstate them without verification. The interaction is plausible in default workflows, though not inherently action-taking.
conditions: IF the user treats awesome-nlp entries as authoritative facts inside Perplexity, errors can cascade into generated answers.
IF Perplexity outputs are reused without human verification, downstream mistakes can persist.
mitigations: Verify any facts from awesome-nlp before reusing them.
Ask Perplexity for sources, not just summaries.
Cross-check critical claims against primary sources.
Do not automate decisions from Perplexity output alone.
requires-engineering: add citation validation before downstream use.

E_compliance.rationale: No specific regulated data class or residency mismatch is documented for awesome-nlp, while Perplexity’s privacy policy and vendor-hosted processing imply standard third-party handling of uploaded documents and browsing context. Because the pair does not show a concrete PHI/EU-PII flow, this is a compliance-gap risk rather than a breach by default. The other agent is not cited for residency because it has no such profile fields.
conditions: IF regulated data is uploaded to Perplexity, policy and residency review is required.
IF the workflow requires retention or deletion guarantees, the current profiles do not document them.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in Perplexity unless policy is approved.
Check retention and deletion settings before upload.
Use anonymized inputs for compliance-sensitive work.
Document the data class before each upload.
requires-engineering: obtain a DPA or residency attestation.
